stories.title: Bank of Canada likely to raise rates as inflation hits 3.1%
stories.summary: Canada’s inflation rose to 3.1% in the most recent month, while core inflation stayed subdued. The economy is described as weak and the effect of a new round of tariffs remains unclear. Based on these conditions, most major forecasters now expect the Bank of Canada to raise its key overnight lending rate at its upcoming decision.
stories.why: Inflation data can shift expectations for central-bank interest rates, bond yields, borrowing costs and household purchasing power.

stories.title: US stocks open higher as Anthropic IPO filing draws attention
stories.summary: On Monday, 26 October 2026, U.S. equity markets opened higher, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average up 0.20% to 52,320.45, the S&P 500 up 0.21% to 7,639.7, and the Nasdaq Composite up 0.28% to 26,026.865. Investor focus was on Anthropic’s IPO filing, which disclosed a 1‑for‑1,000 reverse stock split, trailing‑twelve‑month revenue growth of about 1,200% from late 2025 to late 2026, roughly 250 enterprise customers generating over $10 million in revenue, and $161.2 billion in aggregate rent commitments under Broadcom lease arrangements.
stories.why: The filing signals strong investor interest in AI firms and can influence sector sentiment and capital allocation.

stories.title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack
stories.summary: Brown's vocal coach, rapper Omololu Akinlolu, who joined the attack, was sentenced to four months imprisonment, suspended for 12 months. Judge Tony Baumgartner said Brown's use of the glass bottle to hit the victim twice over the head "was plainly dangerous", adding that the violence of the attack was "intense".

stories.title: Nurse killed, health worker injured in Ebola response attack in north‑eastern DRC
stories.summary: A nurse has been killed and another health worker seriously injured when local youths attacked them as they responded to an Ebola alert in north‑eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, accusing them of contaminating water and spreading the virus. The World Health Organization condemned the attack, while neighbouring Uganda banned non‑essential travel to and from the DRC and quarantined returning citizens for 21 days. The outbreak has caused more than 4,800 deaths and nearly 10,000 infections since it began in May.

stories.title: India‑US trade deal moves to fine‑tuning stage, says minister
stories.summary: Minister Piyush Goyal said the India‑United States trade negotiations have entered a fine‑tuning phase, indicating that most of the talks are concluded. The two sides are now working on detailed adjustments before a final agreement is signed. This step brings the bilateral trade framework closer to completion.
